To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we introduce a new request ordering technique called refinable timestamps that enables efficient, transactionally-consistent graph processing in large, distributed graph stores, and demonstrate that this technique can achieve performance comparable to or better than state-of-the-art systems on a variety of graph processing workloads.

(a) Weaver enables efficient, transactionally consistent, dynamic graph analyses; (b) Weaver achieves high performance on a variety of dynamic graph workloads; (c) Weaver’s refinable timestamps enable efficient transactional consistency for dynamic graphs; (d) Weaver’s refinements can be applied to existing systems to improve their performance and consistency.

(a) we introduce the Weaver graph store, a new system that combines strict serializability and horizontal scalability; (b) we introduce the concept of refinable timestamps, a novel request ordering technique that enables Weaver to achieve high performance; (c) Weaver achieves 12× better throughput than Titan, 4× lower tail latency than GraphLab and 8× better throughput than Blockchain.info; (d) Weaver can scale to hundreds of machines and support millions of transactions per second;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a distributed graph store that enables efficient, transactionally consistent graph analyses on a single, dynamic graph.
the design and implementation of a highperformance graph store that supports both dynamic and static graphs and enables efficient, transaction-based graph analyses on large-scale data.
the problem of how to design a scalable, high-performance, and consistent graph store.
